question: If left{((sec θ-1)/(sec θ+1))right}{ⁿ} = cosec θ - cot θ, then n = ?
solution:
**Given:**

 left{((sec θ-1)/(sec θ+1))right}{ⁿ} = cosec θ - cot θ

**Formula Used:**

sec θ = (1)/(cos θ )

cosec θ = (1)/(sin θ )

cot θ = (cos theta)/(sin theta )

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

As, we know sec θ = (1)/(cos θ ) , cosec θ = (1)/(sin θ ) , cot θ = (cos theta)/(sin theta )

So, left{((sec θ-1)/(sec θ+1))right}{ⁿ} = cosec θ - cot θ

⇒ {(1)/(cos θ) - 1 over(1)/(cos θ ) + 1 }ⁿ = 1over sinθ - cosθ over sinθ 

⇒ {1- cosθ over cosθ × cosθ over cosθ + 1 }ⁿ = ((1 - cos theta ))/(sin theta)

⇒ {1 - cosθ over 1 + cosθ }ⁿ = ((1 - cos theta ))/(sin theta)

⇒ {( 1- cosθ) times ( 1- cosθ) over ( 1 + cosθ) times ( 1- cosθ) }ⁿ = ( 1 - cos θ) over ( sin θ)

⇒ {(1 - cos θ)² over ( 1 - cos² θ)}ⁿ = ( 1 - cos θ) over sin θ

⇒ { ( 1 - cos θ ) ²over sin² θ}ⁿ = ( 1 - cos θ)over sin θ 

So, n = (1)/(2) or 0.5 only satisfies this equation 

Hence,** the correct answer is option 2).**
